wakesMostNights.definition: As part of its own printed ability's normal routine, the player is woken by the Storyteller on most nights of the game (every night, or every night after the first) to act or to receive information. Waking only on night 1, only once, only on a condition that usually doesn't hold (the King, Godfather, Zombuul, Cult Leader's alignment change), only after death, or only to meet the evil team doesn't count. Characters whose waking depends on a borrowed, believed or script-dependent ability (Alchemist, Amnesiac, Cannibal, Apprentice, Drunk, Marionette, Hermit) are not tagged. Lil' Monsta counts, because the Minions wake every night to choose its babysitter.

neverChooses.definition: The character's own ability is fully passive: it never asks its player to make any decision, at night or by day. No choosing players, characters or options, no optional actions, guesses, statements, claims or performances, and no special use of nominations or votes. The Mutant's madness requirement and choices made by other players or the Storyteller don't count against it. Characters who may hold, borrow or believe they have a choosing ability (Alchemist, Apprentice, Cannibal, Pixie, Amnesiac, Drunk, Marionette, Hermit, Lunatic) are not tagged.

boundToAnotherPlayer.definition: The ability sets up an ongoing pairing with one particular other player: the character serves, guards, inherits from, mirrors, feeds on, arms or takes their alignment from that person, so that the partner's fate, votes or alignment shape the character's game. Covers the Butler's master, the Evil Twin's twin, the Grandmother's grandchild, the Pixie's known Townsfolk, the Choirboy's King, the Ogre's chosen player, the Lleech's host, the Gnome's amigo, the Scarlet Woman's Demon (whom she replaces) and the Boffin's Demon (whom it arms). Seat neighbours, a fresh target each night, a one-off choice, or merely being known by the Demon (King, Lunatic, Marionette) don't count.

choosesPlayersAtNight.definition: The character's own printed ability has its player choose one or more players (not characters, not options) at night, even if only once, conditionally or on death (Ravenkeeper, Godfather, Zombuul, Ogre's first night). Lil' Monsta counts, because the Minions choose its babysitter each night. Choosing characters (Engineer, Courtier, Philosopher, Ojo), choosing by day, and abilities that depend on a borrowed, believed or script-dependent ability (Alchemist, Apprentice, Cannibal, Drunk, Marionette, Hermit) don't count.

harmsOwnTeam.definition: The printed ability (excluding [setup] text) has a built-in drawback that can work against the player's own team: it can kill, execute, drunk or poison the player or a teammate (the Minstrel's table-wide drunkenness counts), lose their team the game, restrict their own voting, give the opposing team information or power (the Poppy Grower's death lets evil find each other), or make them misjudge or misplay for their side. Every Outsider qualifies. Unreliable information alone (e.g. the Fortune Teller's red herring) and redirecting a death that was already coming (the Mayor) don't count.

needsDeathToAct.definition: The ability lies dormant until a death: it does nothing at all until the character itself dies or is executed (Saint, Goblin, Boomdandy), or until a particular death happens (an executee, the Demon, the King, a Minion by execution), or it can only work on players who are already dead (Professor, Bone Collector). Abilities with any effect while everyone lives (start-of-game info, ongoing protection, nightly kills) don't count.

changesTheRules.definition: The ability changes a standing procedural rule of the game for the whole table, every day it is in force: who may nominate or vote, how votes are cast or counted, what an execution does, whether players may move or talk privately, or whether the Storyteller must follow the rules. One-off personal overrides (Judge), extra or special nominations for one player (Butcher, Banshee, Golem), effects on chosen players (Thief, Devil's Advocate) and pure win or loss conditions (Heretic, Vortox, Leviathan, Mastermind) don't count. The Vizier counts: every vote in which good takes part can end in an immediate execution.

oneShot.definition: The player gets exactly one deliberate use of their ability in the whole game (a single choice, guess, question, wish, nomination or declaration) and then it is spent: once-per-game actions, single-day actions (Juggler, Princess), first-night-only choices (Ogre, Widow), a single fixed night (Summoner) or a single choice on death (Ravenkeeper, Klutz, Moonchild). Passive triggers and repeatable actions don't count.
